data.description:
## Observation
During the comment-remediation epic on 2026-10-22 PDT, multiple MCP tracker writes (leaf close, progress comments, and an inventory edit) timed out after 91–181 seconds waiting for the tickets write lock. The holder was `op=compact-sweep`. Read-only SSM checks found two successive detached sweeps running for 33:46 and 11:00 respectively, with `git log --full-history` children under them. Targeted SIGTERM to each optional sweep process group released the lock; the next leaf close and comment writes succeeded. Rebar's lock error says interrupted sweep events stay live. This is a repeated write outage, not a proven root cause.

## Hypotheses
A per-ticket authorship fallback may still walk Git history while holding the lock; Git or disk activity may stall; the between-ticket yield check may miss a writer waiting to acquire the lock. These remain unproven. Compare the shipped mesodermic-vaporish-seaslug fix before calling this a regression.

## Experiment and acceptance
Reproduce with an instrumented sweep and concurrent writer; record lock acquisition/release, Git child state, and whether a pending writer makes the sweep yield. Fix the confirmed cause so optional compaction does not make ordinary tracker writes exceed their lock deadline. Preserve crash-atomic per-ticket folds, verify interruption loses no events, and add a focused regression check. No code changes are part of the comment-remediation epic.
data.title: MCP compaction sweep can hold tracker writes past their lock deadline
